## Summary

The business-day roll now skips public holidays as well as weekends. I made the change in a single file, `BusinessDay.java`:

- Added a `HOLIDAYS` set with the five fixed 2026 dates (2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28).
- Changed `onOrAfter` from a weekend-only ternary to a loop that advances one day at a time while the date is a weekend **or** a listed holiday, correctly chaining across adjacent non-business days (e.g. a holiday falling on a Friday rolls past the weekend too).

**Structural impact kept minimal:** `BusinessDay` is a tiny utility class — its only other method is a private no-op constructor (CC 1), so `WMC_other` is ~1 and just one file was touched. All three callers (`BuildOwner`, `RejectDailyLimit`, `BulkSignup`) were left untouched since they call `onOrAfter` unchanged. The test suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`), including the acceptance test whose helper already models the holiday-skipping behaviour.

## Summary

The business-day roll now skips public holidays as well as weekends. I made the change in a single file, `BusinessDay.java`:

- Added a `HOLIDAYS` set with the five fixed 2026 dates (2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28).
- Changed `onOrAfter` from a weekend-only ternary to a loop that advances one day at a time while the date is a weekend **or** a listed holiday, correctly chaining across adjacent non-business days (e.g. a holiday falling on a Friday rolls past the weekend too).

**Structural impact kept minimal:** `BusinessDay` is a tiny utility class — its only other method is a private no-op constructor (CC 1), so `WMC_other` is ~1 and just one file was touched. All three callers (`BuildOwner`, `RejectDailyLimit`, `BulkSignup`) were left untouched since they call `onOrAfter` unchanged. The test suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`), including the acceptance test whose helper already models the holiday-skipping behaviour.
